sec: Causes of the immune picture, complications, modified Duke major criteria

items.q: Causes listed for the immune/vasculitic picture — match — 1) Low C3 and C4 2) Others … A) Hepatitis C virus, cryoglobulinaemia, leprosy B) Infective endocarditis
items.exp: 'Causes : · IE (↓C3, ↓C4), · Hep C Virus, · Cryoglobulinemia, · Leprosy'. (Book p1050)

items.q: Cardiac complications — match — 1) Stroke / ACS 2) Heart failure 3) Perivalvular abscess … A) Due to valvular insufficiency with new-onset adult AR / MR B) Common in aortic position, causes conduction block C) Fragment embolisation into coronaries
items.exp: 'Stroke / ACS : Fragment embolization into coronaries'; 'Heart failure : d/t Valvular insufficiency, New onset adult AR/MR'; 'Perivalvular abscess : (Common in aorta) → Conduction block'. (Book p1050)

items.q: Non-cardiac complications — match the group — 1) Embolic 2) Immunological 3) Septic … A) Metastatic infection, mycotic aneurysm B) Embolic occlusion C) Immunological phenomena
items.exp: 'Non-cardiac complications : · Embolic occlusion, · Immunological, · metastatic infection, · mycotic aneurysm'. (Book p1050)

items.q: Right-sided IE complications — match — 1) Pulmonary 2) Cardiac 3) Vascular … A) Right heart failure B) Pulmonary abscess, empyema C) Mycotic aneurysm of pulmonary artery
items.exp: 'Right-sided IE complications : · Pulmonary abscess, Empyema, · Right heart failure, · mycotic aneurysm of pulmonary artery'. (Book p1050)

items.q: Which organism group is printed as a cause of perivalvular abscess with conduction block?
opts: Perivalvular abscess is common in the aortic position
It is common in the tricuspid position
It is common in the pulmonary position
It is common in the mitral position
items.exp: 'Perivalvular abscess : (Common in aorto) → Conduction block'. (Book p1050)

items.q: Modified Duke criteria — match the combinations — 1) Definite by majors 2) Major plus minors 3) Minors only … A) 1 major + 3 minor B) 5 minor C) 2 major
items.exp: 'Criterias : 2 major OR 1 major + 3 minor OR 5 minor'. (Book p1050)

items.q: How many minor criteria are required to satisfy the modified Duke criteria on their own?
Fill up (Blood-culture technique): '______ sets (______ ml each) from 3 sites.'
items.exp: 'Blood culture : · 3 sets (20 ml each) from 3 sites'. (Book p1050)

items.q: Blood-culture volumes and timing — match — 1) Per bottle 2) Interval between sets 3) Repeat interval … A) 30-60 minutes B) 18-24 hours C) 10 ml aerobic plus 10 ml anaerobic
items.exp: 'Blood (10 ml aerobic + 10 ml anaerobic) taken over 30-60 minutes'; 'Culture to be repeated every 18-24 hours'. (Book p1050)

items.q: How does the page define a positive blood-culture major criterion for typical organisms?
opts: Typical organism (MRSA, Streptococcus viridans) from two separate cultures
Any single culture growing a skin commensal
Three cultures drawn from one venipuncture
items.exp: 'Positive culture : Typical organism (mRSA, Strep. viridans) from 2 separate cultures'. (Book p1050)

items.q: Which organisms are named as needing only a single positive culture or antibody detection?
items.exp: 'HACeK group (Coxiella burnetii) single positive culture or antibodies detected'. (Book p1050)

items.q: Judge the major criteria: I Three sets of 20 ml from three sites are required. II Persistently positive cultures also count as a major criterion.
items.exp: '3 sets (20 ml each) from 3 sites' and 'Persistently positive culture' are both printed. (Book p1050)
